approach: Because no author code is released, reproduce the target by reimplementing the Interconnectedness Coefficient exactly from Eq. (1)-(6) using finite simple graphs and fractions.Fraction for all synthetic checks. Construct the hub-extended bridge family Hp,q,r from Section 4, evaluate every vertex in V>=2, and assert that the connector x has IC(x)=2/3 and is the unique strict maximizer. Validate the implementation with Bp,q, the single-cohesion-defect variants, Eq. (3) vs Eq. (6) cross-checks, gateway competitor bounds, and r-invariance of IC(x). Write exact fractions and pass/fail flags to results/metrics.json; the HIM empirical analysis is optional and is attempted only if the exact edgelist is present.

files.purpose: Define a simple undirected graph class that rejects self-loops/duplicates, computes degree and candidate set V>=2, ordinary local clustering Eq. (1), leave-one-out clustering by explicit neighborhood removal Eq. (3) and by triangle/common-neighbor formula Eq. (6), mean CLOO Eq. (4), IC Eq. (5), exact max/uniqueness checks, and the IC=1 equality-condition test. Use fractions.Fraction for synthetic graphs and a float mode only for optional large empirical graphs.

Build synthetic graph families Bp,q, Hp,q,r, and defective Bp,q with one removed non-gateway left-clique edge, using deterministic labels and exact edge sets from Section 4. Validate vertex/edge counts against formulas. Optionally include Jc,h,r only if needed; it is not required for target C1.

Run primary C1 checks on Hp,q,r instances: IC(x)=2/3 exactly, x is the unique strict maximizer over V>=2, hub s has IC=0, leaves are omitted, IC(x) is invariant to r, and gateway competitors obey the bound. Also run C2-C4 sanity checks, Eq. (3) vs Eq. (6) cross-checks, and write results/metrics.json.

Single CLI entrypoint. Default execution runs the full synthetic verification and writes results/metrics.json. --smoke runs only H(3,3,1) and B(4,3) to prove the data flow. No external packages are required beyond the Python standard library.

claim_scope.reason: C1 is the exact synthetic theorem target; C2-C4 cheaply validate the implementation. C5 construction is not needed for C1 and HIM is optional only if the exact graph is available.

arithmetic.uniqueness_rule: strict exact Fraction comparison; no tie allowed among V>=2 for C1

defect_instances.remove_edge_between: first two deterministic non-gateway left-clique vertices
first two deterministic non-gateway left-clique vertices

config.candidate_rule: degree >= 2 (V>=2); omit degree-0 and degree-1 vertices from ranking/output
config.leave_one_out_rule: C_u_after_removing_v = 0 if d(u)<3 else 2*(T(u)-|N(u) intersection N(v)|)/((d(u)-1)*(d(u)-2)), where T(u)=e(N(u))
config.cloo_rule: CLOO(v)=mean over all u in N(v) of C_u_after_removing_v, including d(u)<3 neighbors as 0

steps: Create the project skeleton with results/ and optional data/ directories. Do not download anything for C1; only standard-library Python is needed.

Implement ic_measure.py: a SimpleGraph class with adjacency dicts of sets, add_edge rejecting self-loops and duplicate edges, degree(), candidates() for V>=2, local_clustering() per Eq. (1), edges_inside() for T(u), leave_one_out_explicit() per Eq. (3), leave_one_out_formula() per Eq. (6), cloo() per Eq. (4), and ic() per Eq. (5). Return fractions.Fraction in exact mode.

Implement ic_measure.py helpers: all_ic() returning candidate scores, unique_maximizer() checking a strict exact gap, and max_equality_condition() testing the Proposition 1 condition IC=1 iff C(v)=0 and every adjacent leave-one-out term is 1.

Implement graph_families.py: make_B(p,q) with clique Kp containing a, disjoint clique Kq containing b, connector x adjacent to a and b, and no a-b edge; make_H(p,q,r) by adding hub s adjacent to x and r leaves; make_defect_B(p,q) by removing the first deterministic non-gateway left-clique edge. Validate simple graph invariants and expected counts.
For Hp,q,r, validate formula counts: |V|=p+q+r+2, |E|=p(p-1)/2+q(q-1)/2+r+3, and candidate count excludes only the r degree-1 leaves. For Bp,q, validate |V|=p+q+1 and |E|=p(p-1)/2+q(q-1)/2+2.

Implement verify_claims.py. For each Hp,q,r instance, build the graph, compute all candidate IC values exactly, assert IC(x)=Fraction(2,3), assert x is the unique strict maximizer, assert hub s has IC=0, assert leaves are omitted, and assert IC(x) is unchanged for r in [1,2,5,10] with p=q=3.

In verify_claims.py, additionally check gateway competitors in Hp,q,r: gateway IC must be 0 when its clique size m=3 and 2(m-1)/m^2 when m>=4, and must be <=3/8, hence strictly below 2/3. Record the runner-up and exact gap.

In verify_claims.py, run C2-C4 sanity checks: Bp,q must have IC(x)=1 and satisfy the Proposition 1 equality condition; the defective Bp,q with p=4 must have IC(x)=5/6 exactly; the defective Bp,q with p=10 must have IC(x)=71/72 exactly.
Cross-check leave_one_out_explicit() against leave_one_out_formula() exactly on small graphs H(3,3,1), B(4,3), and the p=4 defect graph. Fail if any exact Fraction differs.

Implement reproduce.py with argparse. Default runs verify_claims.run_all() and writes results/metrics.json. --smoke runs only H(3,3,1) and B(4,3), writes results/smoke_metrics.json, and prints a concise summary.
Run the smoke command and inspect: H(3,3,1) must have |V|=9, |E|=10, 8 candidates, IC(x)=2/3, unique maximizer x; B(4,3) must have IC(x)=1.

Run the full synthetic verification with python reproduce.py. Confirm results/metrics.json contains the C1 exact value '2/3', decimal 0.6666666667, maximizer 'x', unique=true, runner-up value, gap, and passed=true.

If data/him.edgelist exists, optionally compute HIM statistics in float mode and record whether vertex/edge counts and mean clustering match 9222/36324/0.114. If it does not exist, mark HIM as skipped and do not let it block C1.

Inspect results/metrics.json for C1-C4 status, exact fractions, instance table, and the Eq. (3)-vs-Eq. (6) cross-check flag. The final reported C1 number is the decimal approximation of the exact Fraction(2,3).
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`. It builds only H(3,3,1) and B(4,3), prints vertex/edge counts, candidate counts, IC(x), hub IC, runner-up, exact fractions, and writes results/smoke_metrics.json. Success requires H(3,3,1): |V|=9, |E|=10, 8 candidates, IC(x)=2/3 exactly and uniquely maximal; B(4,3): IC(x)=1 exactly.
intermediate_checks: H(3,3,1) has |V|=9, |E|=10, exactly 1 degree-1 leaf, and 8 candidates in V>=2.
Hp,q,r candidate set contains the p+q clique vertices, x, and s, but not the r leaves; hub s has IC=0 exactly.
H(3,3,1) gives IC(x)=2/3 exactly, and the runner-up is a gateway with exact value 0 or <=3/8; no tie with x.
H(3,3,1), H(3,4,1), H(4,3,2), H(4,4,1), H(5,5,3), and H(10,10,1) all give IC(x)=2/3 and unique maximizer x.
r-invariance: with p=q=3, IC(x)=2/3 exactly for r=1,2,5,10.
B(4,3) has |V|=8, |E|=11, IC(x)=1 exactly, C(x)=0, and both adjacent leave-one-out terms equal 1.
Defect p=4 gives IC(x)=5/6 exactly; defect p=10 gives IC(x)=71/72 exactly.
Eq. (3) explicit neighborhood removal and Eq. (6) triangle/common-neighbor formula agree exactly on H(3,3,1), B(4,3), and the p=4 defect graph.
No self-loops or duplicate edges are present in any synthetic graph; all graph invariants match the closed-form vertex/edge counts.
Metrics contain exact fraction strings and decimal approximations; C1 value is reported on [0,1], not as a percentage.
budget_plan: Total budget ~10 minutes CPU. Spend ~4-5 minutes writing the four Python files and validating graph invariants, <1 minute on the smoke run, <1 minute on the full synthetic C1-C4 run, and ~2 minutes inspecting results/metrics.json. Optional HIM parsing gets at most 1-2 minutes and only if data/him.edgelist already exists. Keep ~1 minute reserve. The full synthetic computation is seconds; no GPU or downloads are needed.
